definitions.explanation: Acting or doing something slowly and without energy or motivation. Often implies wasting time.
Liquid flowing continuously in a slow stream.

examples.japanese: {休日|きゅうじつ}はだらだら{過|す}ごしてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up spending my day off lazing around.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}がだらだらと{長引|ながび}いた。
だらだらテレビを{見|み}ていたら、もう{夜|よる}になっていた。
examples.english: I was lazily watching TV, and before I knew it, it was already night.

examples.japanese: {話|はなし}がだらだらと{続|つづ}いて、いつ{終|お}わるのか{分|わ}からなかった。
examples.english: The talk dragged on and on, and I had no idea when it would end.

examples.japanese: {汗|あせ}がだらだら{流|なが}れた。
{血|ち}がだらだらと{出|で}ている。
{鼻血|はなぢ}がだらだら{止|と}まらない。
{暑|あつ}くて{額|ひたい}から{汗|あせ}がだらだらと{垂|た}れてきた。
examples.english: It was hot and sweat started dripping down from my forehead.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}した{後|あと}、{背中|せなか}を{汗|あせ}がだらだらと{流|なが}れて、シャツが{濡|ぬ}れてしまった。
examples.english: After exercising, sweat was dripping down my back and my shirt got soaked.

notes:
だらだら is an onomatopoeic word with two main uses. The more common sense describes lazy, aimless, or drawn-out behavior, often with a negative connotation of wasting time. The second sense describes liquid dripping or trickling slowly and continuously.

COMMON PATTERNS (sense 1 — lazily):
- だらだら{過|す}ごす: to spend time lazily
- だらだらと{長引|ながび}く: to drag on
- だらだらする: to laze around, to be idle
- だらだら{続|つづ}く: to go on and on without purpose

COMMON PATTERNS (sense 2 — dripping):
- {汗|あせ}がだらだら{流|なが}れる: sweat dripping down
- {血|ち}がだらだら{出|で}る: blood trickling continuously

CONTRAST:
- きびきび: briskly, energetically (opposite of sense 1)
- てきぱき: efficiently, promptly (opposite of sense 1)
- ぽたぽた: drip-drip (drops falling one by one, vs. だらだら's continuous flow)
